name: Kärrtorp Junction
region: Närke, on the plain south of Örebro
description: Ten years ago Kärrtorp was a parish of farms on the flat Närke plain; then the western main line came through, a junction was built where the branch to Örebro meets it, and a town of railway workers, merchants and hotels has grown up around the station. New wooden houses stand on lots between old farms, and the church bell competes with the station bell. The farmers grumble about the smoke and the newcomers but sell them milk and hay.
seasonNotes: November, the darkest and dreariest month. Low clouds lie over the plain, it rains or sleets most days, and the roads are rivers of mud. It is dark by half past three, and paraffin lamps burn around the station from mid-afternoon. Locomotives' smoke hangs in the wet air. Farmers are threshing and slaughtering; Martinmas brings goose dinners and the end of the servants' year, when hired hands change places.
travel: From Uppsala by rail via Stockholm and the western main line, about seven hours; one of the best-connected places in the country.
publicFacts: The western main line reached Kärrtorp in 1862 and the branch line to Örebro opened in 1866, making it a junction.
The railway hotel by the station is the best in the district and travellers stay there between trains.
The State Railways employ more than a hundred men at Kärrtorp: engine drivers, firemen, switchmen and workshop hands.
The marsh east of the town was partly drained for the railway embankment and floods every autumn.
The old farmers and the railway people sit on opposite sides of the church.
A free church congregation has started meeting in a hall near the station, to the vicar's displeasure.
The town's lending library was founded by the stationmaster and is open on Wednesday and Saturday evenings.
At Martinmas, servants leave their old places and new ones arrive with their chests on the trains.

places.name: Kärrtorp Junction Station
places.ownerRole: the station master of the junction
places.description: The station is a large brick building with a tower clock and a long covered platform, the busiest place for many miles. Trains arrive in clouds of steam and sparks, the bell rings, and porters push trolleys of luggage through the puddles. The telegraph clatters in the office day and night. Coal smoke, wet iron and the smell of paraffin lamps fill the dark afternoon.

places.name: The Railway Hotel

places.description: The railway hotel faces the station, a new three-storey building with plaster ornaments and a dining room with white tablecloths. Travellers wait there between trains, reading newspapers by the stove. The smell of coffee, cigars and roasting goose fills the lobby at Martinmas. Through the windows the lamps of the trains pass slowly in the rain.

places.name: Kärrtorp Church
places.description: The old church stands on a slight rise among the farms, a quarter of an hour's walk from the station, its tower visible across the flat fields. The churchyard is muddy and the lime trees drip. Inside, the old box pews are full of farming families, the railway families in the new benches at the back. Damp has stained the plaster around the windows.

places.name: Kärrtorp Parsonage
places.ownerRole: the vicar of the parish, who lives here and serves the church
places.description: The parsonage is an old red farmhouse beside the church, larger than the farms around it. Sleet blows against its windows. In the yard the glebe farm's hands are threshing. The vicar's study is crowded with visitors at Martinmas, coming to collect their moving certificates.

places.name: Lindqvist's Smithy
places.ownerRole: the smith of the Lindqvist family, who gave the smithy its name
places.description: The smithy is on the old road where it crosses the railway, busier than ever with carts, wagons and the railway's small jobs. Two hearths burn and the smith has an apprentice and a striker. The light of the forge spills out onto the wet road. The clang of the hammer is drowned out every time a train passes.

places.name: Kärrtorp Lending Library
places.ownerRole: the keeper of the lending library, the schoolmaster
places.description: The lending library occupies two rooms in a new wooden building near the station, warm and lamplit on its open evenings. Railway workers and clerks sit at the long table with newspapers and books. Rain drums on the window. The librarian, a retired schoolmaster, peers over his spectacles at everyone who enters.

places.name: Kärrtorp Gård
places.ownerRole: a freeholder farming family, the oldest in the parish
places.description: The old farm that gave the town its name now stands with railway sidings at the bottom of its fields. The house is a solid two-storey building with old outbuildings, and the family refuses to sell to the railway company. The threshing goes on in the barn and the sound mixes with the trains. Geese are being fattened in a pen for Martinmas.

places.description: A small grey cottage stands at the edge of the marsh where the embankment cuts across it, the trains thundering past within a stone's throw. The ground around it is waterlogged every autumn. A family of railway navvies lives there now, with the cow sold. The windows rattle at every train.
